message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling “detailed” information about a network interface (or *device connector* in some contexts). I’ll cover the most common ways—CLI tools, system files, and a few programmatic APIs—so you can pick the one that fits your workflow. --- ## 1️⃣ Command‑Line (Linux) | Tool | What it shows | Typical usage | |------|---------------|---------------| | **`ip`** (`ip addr show`) | IP addresses, MTU, flags, state, MAC, etc. | `ip addr show eth0` | | **`ifconfig`** | Legacy but still useful; shows IP, netmask, broadcast, RX/TX bytes, errors, etc. | `ifconfig eth0` | | **`ethtool`** | Driver name, firmware version, speed/duplex, supported modes, statistics counters. | `ethtool -i eth0` – driver info
`ethtool -S eth0` – stats | | **`lshw`** | Full hardware description (driver, bus info, capabilities). | `sudo lshw -class network -short` | | **`nmcli`** (NetworkManager) | Connection status, DNS, routes, etc. | `nmcli device show eth0` | | **`ss`** | Socket statistics per interface. | `ss -i` | | **`netstat`** | Old‑school socket stats. | `netstat -i` | ### Example: Get everything you need for `eth0` ```bash # Basic interface info ip addr show eth0 # Driver & firmware ethtool -i eth0 # Supported link modes ethtool -a eth0 # autonegotiation ethtool -k eth0 # offload settings # Statistics counters ethtool -S eth0 # Hardware tree sudo lshw -class network -short # System files (for quick checks) cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address # MAC cat /sys/class/net/eth0/speed # Current negotiated speed cat /sys/class/net/eth0/operstate # up/down ``` --- ## 2️⃣ Command‑Line (macOS) | Tool | What it shows | Typical usage | |------|---------------|---------------| | **`ifconfig`** | Same as Linux but with BSD flavor. | `ifconfig en0` | | **`networksetup`** | Interface configuration, DNS, proxies. | `networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` | | **`system_profiler SPHardwareDataType`** | Detailed hardware specs. | `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType` | | **`scutil --dns`** | DNS resolution details. | `scutil --dns` | Example: ```bash ifconfig en0 ethtool -i en0 # Not available on macOS; use `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` ``` --- ## 3️⃣ Command‑Line (Windows) | PowerShell cmdlet | What it shows | Typical usage | |-------------------|---------------|---------------| | **`Get-NetAdapter`** | Adapter properties, status, MAC, speed. | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet` | | **`Get-NetIPConfiguration`** | IP config, DNS, gateway. | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet` | | **`Get-NetTCPConnection`** | TCP sockets per adapter. | `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess` | | **`Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter`** | WMI view of adapters. | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter | Where-Object {$_.NetEnabled}` | Example: ```powershell Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List * Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet | Format-List * ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Programmatic Access ### Python (cross‑platform) ```python import psutil # Addresses addrs = psutil.net_if_addrs() print(addrs['eth0']) # list of snicaddr objects # Stats stats = psutil.net_if_stats() print(stats['eth0']) # snicstats object # Bytes transmitted/received io_counters = psutil.net_io_counters(pernic=True) print(io_counters['eth0']) ``` ### Go (Linux) ```go package main import ( "fmt" "net" ) func main() { ifaces, _ := net.Interfaces() for _, iface := range ifaces { fmt.Printf("%s: %v\n", iface.Name, iface.Flags) } } ``` ### C/C++ (Linux) ```c #include #include #include #include #include #include int main(void) { struct ifreq ifr; int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0); strcpy(ifr.ifr_name, "eth0"); ioctl(fd, SIOCGIFFLAGS, &ifr); printf("Flags: %x\n", ifr.ifr_flags); close(fd); return 0; } ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Using SNMP (for remote devices) ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable ``` This will dump all rows of the interface table, including index, description, type, speed, admin status, oper status, etc. --- ## 6️⃣ Quick “All‑in‑One” Bash Script ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IF=$1 [ -z "$IF" ] && { echo "Usage: $0 "; exit 1; } echo "=== Basic info ===" ip addr show "$IF" echo "=== Driver info ===" ethtool -i "$IF" echo "=== Offloads ===" ethtool -k "$IF" echo "=== Statistics ===" ethtool -S "$IF" echo "=== Sysfs entries ===" printf "MAC: %s\n" "$(cat /sys/class/net/$IF/address)" printf "Speed: %s\n" "$(cat /sys/class/net/$IF/speed)" printf "OperState: %s\n" "$(cat /sys/class/net/$IF/operstate)" ``` Run it with `./script.sh eth0`. --- ## TL;DR | Platform | One‑liner for “detailed” info | |----------|--------------------------------| | Linux | `ip addr show eth0 && ethtool -i eth0 && ethtool -S eth0` | | macOS | `ifconfig en0 && system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` | | Windows | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List *` | | Python | `psutil.net_if_addrs(); psutil.net_if_stats()` | Pick the method that best matches your environment and needs. If you’re looking for something else (e.g., a specific API call in a particular SDK), let me know!
